title: Retrieval & RAG
blurb: How LLMs get access to knowledge they weren't trained on. Embeddings, vector stores, hybrid search, reranking, chunking, the architecture patterns that actually work, and how to evaluate any of it.

nodes.label: Embeddings (text, multimodal)
nodes.description: Modern embedding models (text and multimodal), how to choose one, what dimensions and pooling mean, why bigger isn't always better.
nodes.doneWhen: You can pick an embedding model for a task, defend the choice, and run an A/B against an alternative.

nodes.label: Vector stores
nodes.description: pgvector, FAISS, Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, Milvus. ANN indexes (HNSW, IVF), filtering, hybrid storage. The right choice depends on scale and operational reality.
nodes.doneWhen: You can pick a vector store for a deployment and explain its index choice.

nodes.label: Hybrid search (BM25 + vector)
nodes.description: Why BM25 still beats vector on exact-match queries, why combining the two is the practical default, score fusion (RRF).
nodes.doneWhen: You can implement BM25 + dense hybrid search with reciprocal rank fusion and measure its lift.

nodes.label: Reranking
nodes.description: Cross-encoders, ColBERT-style late interaction, LLM rerankers. Why retrieval+rerank is almost always better than retrieval alone.
nodes.doneWhen: You can add a reranker to a retrieval pipeline and measure recall-at-k vs precision-at-k changes.

nodes.label: Chunking strategies
nodes.description: Fixed-size, sentence, recursive, semantic, structure-aware. The most-overlooked lever in a mediocre RAG system.
nodes.doneWhen: You can run a chunking-size sweep and report which choice wins on your evaluation set.

nodes.label: Document parsing (PDF, HTML, OCR)
nodes.description: Where most production RAG systems lose accuracy. Layout-aware PDF parsers, HTML cleanup, OCR for scans, table extraction.
nodes.doneWhen: You can build a parser that turns a messy corpus of PDFs and HTML into clean, structured text.

nodes.label: Query reformulation & expansion
nodes.description: HyDE, multi-query, decomposition, step-back prompting. Letting the model rewrite the query before retrieval.
nodes.doneWhen: You can add a query-rewriting step to a RAG pipeline and measure its effect on retrieval quality.

nodes.label: RAG architecture patterns
nodes.description: Naive RAG, modular RAG, agentic RAG, multi-hop retrieval, query routing. The decision tree from 'simplest works' to 'this case justifies complexity'.
nodes.doneWhen: You can pick the simplest RAG architecture that meets your accuracy target and defend not making it more complex.

nodes.label: Advanced RAG (contextual retrieval, GraphRAG)
nodes.description: Contextual Retrieval (Anthropic's chunk-prefix trick), GraphRAG (Microsoft), late-chunking, ColBERT, fine-tuned embeddings. The frontier of retrieval research that's already in production.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe Contextual Retrieval and GraphRAG and explain when each is worth the complexity.

nodes.label: RAG evaluation
nodes.description: Faithfulness, context relevance, answer relevance, retrieval recall. ragas, deepeval, the LLM-as-judge approach. Eval is the difference between a RAG demo and a RAG product.
nodes.doneWhen: You have a RAG eval set, a faithfulness metric, and a regression suite that catches index drift.
